item.text: {"diagnosis":"Candidate/bad runs overrepeat ineffective actions—especially clicks, no-ops/waits, and scrolls—rather than changing strategy after no progress.","expected_mechanism":"Detecting unchanged state before retrying interrupts action loops and forces replanning or termination. Success should improve through fewer wasted operations and more strategy changes; cost is one state comparison and brief replan per suspected retry, with possible delay when repetition is genuinely necessary.","policy_text":"Before repeating an action after no observable progress, compare the current state with the prior state. If unchanged, do not retry unchanged parameters: inspect the failure, alter the target or method, or stop with a concise explanation. Permit repetition only with an explicit new hypothesis.","quantitative_evidence":[{"command":"jq -s 'def r:[.stack_frames[]|select(startswith(\"result:\"))][0]; {bad:([.[]|select(.value>0 and r==\"result:repeated\")|.value]|add),good:([.[]|select(.value<0 and r==\"result:repeated\")|(-.value)]|add),excess:([.[]|select(r==\"result:repeated\")|.value]|add)}' samples.jsonl","finding":"Repeated results total 1,485 bad versus 224 good operations, a +1,261 bad excess and 6.63× raw count."},{"command":"jq -s '{bad_total:([.[]|select(.value>0)|.value]|add),good_total:([.[]|select(.value<0)|(-.value)]|add)}' samples.jsonl","finding":"There are 7,366 bad and 3,780 good operations overall; repetition therefore represents 20.16% of bad operations versus 5.93% of good operations, a 3.40× proportional overrepresentation."},{"command":"jq -s 'def r:[.stack_frames[]|select(startswith(\"result:\"))][0]; def a:[.stack_frames[]|select(startswith(\"action:\"))][0]; [.[]|select(r==\"result:repeated\")]|group_by(a)|map({action:(.[0]|a),bad:([.[]|select(.value>0)|.value]|add//0),good:([.[]|select(.value<0)|(-.value)]|add//0)})|sort_by(-(.bad-.good))' samples.jsonl","finding":"The largest repeated-action imbalances are click 679/40, noop 441/85, and scroll 278/1 (bad/good), showing recurrence across multiple action types."}]}
